key_insight: Among HVOF-sprayed cermet coatings on 65G steel, WC–Co–Cr delivered the best overall structure–property balance, combining the densest microstructure, highest hardness, and lowest friction.
engineering_relevance: For wear-critical machine, power, and metallurgy components, powder/binder selection in HVOF directly controls coating densification, adhesion, hardness, and tribological performance.
method: Compared five HVOF coating systems: WC–Co–Cr, WC–NiCr, WC–Ni, Cr3C2–NiCr, and Al2O3–NiCr.
Evaluated microstructure by SEM/EDS plus microhardness, surface roughness, friction/wear behavior, and adhesive strength.
Related performance differences to powder composition and binder-phase characteristics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative property data showing WC–Co–Cr at μ = 0.143 and 1316.87 HV, while Al2O3–NiCr had the highest friction (0.630) and lowest hardness (631.59 HV).
watch_item: Results are based on a specific HVOF setup and 65G steel substrate, so coating ranking and adhesion may shift with spray parameters, substrate prep, or service environment.
paper_title: THE EFFECT OF THE COMPOSITION OF METAL-CERAMIC POWDERS ON THE STRUCTURE AND PERFORMANCE PROPERTIES OF COATINGS OBTAINED BY THE HVOF METHOD
